hints: Start total and full at 0 before the loop, and the best-so-far count below any real count, such as -1.
Loop with for crossing in range(1, crossings + 1): so crossing is already the crossing number.
Inside the loop, read the count, add it to the total, and replace the best only when the new count is strictly larger.
ferry.answerNote: The best-so-far starts at -1 so the first crossing always replaces it. Reading the first count before the loop also works.

hints: Read the first line before the loop, and test line != '' in the while header.
Convert with int(line) inside the loop, after the test, and read the next line as the last step of the body.

steps.answerNote: A classic sentinel loop: the read before the loop and the read at the end of the body are the same statement.

steps = 0

cases.name: Example 1: 9875
cases.expected:
9875 -> 29 -> 11 -> 2
Digital root: 2 after 3 steps

cases.name: Example 2: 7
cases.expected:
7
Digital root: 7 after 0 steps

cases.name: Typed 10

10 -> 1
Digital root: 1 after 1 step

cases.name: Typed 19
cases.expected:
19 -> 10 -> 1
Digital root: 1 after 2 steps

cases.name: Typed 0
cases.expected:
0
Digital root: 0 after 0 steps

cases.name: Typed 999999999999
cases.expected:
999999999999 -> 108 -> 9

cases.expected:

hints: The outer loop runs while number >= 10.
Inside it, start total = 0, then loop while number > 0, adding number % 10 and doing number = number // 10.
After the inner loop, set number = total, add ' -> ' + str(number) to the chain and count one step.
digitroot.answerNote: The chain starts as the text of the original number, so it is printed correctly even after the inner loop changes number.

hints: Test size.isdigit() first and combine the tests with and, so int(size) only runs on digits.
For each row, start line = '', loop over the columns adding one character, then print the line after the inner loop.
Test the border first, then the centre n // 2, then the diagonals row == col and row + col == n - 1.
rug.answerNote: The order of the if/elif chain is what keeps the corners as # and the centre as O.

Guess 2: 3

hints: Keep low and high, the smallest and largest numbers still possible; start them at 1 and top.
At the top of while True:, stop with a message if low > high; otherwise print the next guess and read an answer.
Repeat the read while answer != 'h' and answer != 'l' and answer != 'c', then break on c or move low to middle + 1 or high to middle - 1.
guess.answerNote: This is binary search: each answer halves the numbers left, so 100 needs at most 7 guesses.

hints: Let start run over every index and end from start + 2 to len(text), so the run is text[start:end].
